summary_out.hypothesis: FALSIFIED at default parameters. The 'third orthogonal skip gate adds super-linear PnL' hypothesis was disconfirmed for the canonical aggressor-flow-gate parameters: stacking did not improve on chop+spread — it destroyed ~30% of the g2l1 PnL gain. Failure mechanism mirrors island-0's g2l2 chop misfire: gate parameters tuned for one base (aggressor-flow-gate as a standalone gate) do not transfer cleanly when composed onto a different base (vol-regime-sizer already pre-filtered by chop+spread). The 2-contract / 10s threshold is too sensitive for MES tick cadence stacked on an already-aggressive composed pair; the flow axis also appears partly redundant with chop+spread (wide-spread bursts correlate with directional aggressor pressure), so the union of the three gates was larger than the orthogonality hypothesis assumed.
summary_out.next: Two viable g3 directions, in order of expected leverage. (1) RETUNE flow threshold only: raise flow_threshold to 5.0-8.0 contracts and/or shorten flow_window_seconds to 3-5s so the gate fires only on genuine pressure spikes, not ordinary directional drift. This is the parameter-side fix to the verbatim-port failure that island-0 g2l2 documented (chop ported vrs→ptg lost; here flow ported afg→vrs lost — same shape, mechanism generalizable but parameters base-specific). (2) If retuned flow still regresses, the verdict is 'flow axis is fundamentally redundant on vrs base' — pivot to a structurally different third axis: top-of-book size asymmetry (bid_size vs ask_size ratio), which was the alternative explicitly named in the gen-1 migration alongside flow imbalance and remains untested. Recommended g3l1: option (1); g3l2: option (2) if g3l1 regresses. Also: extract per-skip-combination instrumentation counters from per-date stdout into structured analysis before g3 — the redundancy-vs-wrong-threshold question cannot be settled empirically without them, and both hypotheses currently fit the data.
